source_text: λέγει δὲ οὕτως· „ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοὶ, ὑπὲρ τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ (Χριστοῦ) καὶ ἡμῶν ἐπισυναγωγῆς ἐπ᾿ αὐτὸν, εἰς τὸ μὴ σαλευθῆναι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ νοὸς μηδὲ θροεῖσθαι, μήτε διὰ πνεύματος μήτε διὰ λόγου μήτε διὰ ἐπιστολῆς ὡς δι᾿ ἡμῶν, ὡς ὅτι ἐνέστηκεν ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ κυρίου. μή τις ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατήσῃ κατὰ μηδένα τρόπον, ὅτι, ἐὰν μὴ ἔλθῃ ἡ ἀποστασία πρῶτον καὶ ἀποκαλυφθῇ ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας, ὁ ἀντικείμενος καὶ ὑπεραιρόμενος ἐπὶ πάντα λεγόμενον θεὸν ἢ σέβασμα, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καθίσαι, ἀποδεικνύντα ἑαυτὸν ὅτι ἐστὶ θεός. οὐ μνημονεύετε ὅτι ἔτι ὢν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ταῦτ᾿ ἔλεγον ὑμῖν; καὶ νῦν τὸ κατέχον οἴδατε, εἰς τὸ ἀποκαλυφθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ αὐτοῦ καιρῷ· τὸ γὰρ μυστήριον ἤδη ἐνεργεῖται τῆς ἀνομίας, μόνον ὁ κατέχων ἄρτι, ἕως ἐκ μέσου γένηται· καὶ τότε ἀποκαλυφθήσεται ὁ ἄνομος, ὃν ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἀναλοῖ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ καὶ καταργήσει τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, οὗ ἐστιν ἡ παρουσία κατ᾿ ἐνέργειαν τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει καὶ σημείοις καὶ τέρασι ψεύδους καὶ ἐν πάσῃ ἀπάτῃ ἀδικίας τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις, ἀνθ᾿ ὧν τὴν ἀγάπην τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἐδέξαντο εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι αὐτούς. καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πέμπει αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς ἐνέργειαν πλάνης εἰς τὸ πιστεῦσαι αὐτοὺς τῷ ψεύδει, ἵνα κριθῶσιν ἅπαντες οἱ μὴ πιστεύσαντες τῇ ἀληθείᾳ ἀλλ᾿ εὐδοκήσαντες ἐν τῇ ἀδικίᾳ.“ ἕκαστον δὲ τούτων σαφηνίσαι οὐ τῇ παρούσῃ ἁρμόζει πραγματείᾳ. ἡ περὶ αὐτοῦ δὲ προφητεία ἐν τῷ Δανιὴλ λέλεκται, δυναμένη τὸν φρονίμως καὶ εὐγνωμόνως ἀναγινώσκοντα ἐπιστρέψαι ἐπὶ τὸ θαυμάσαι τοὺς λόγους ὡς ἀληθῶς ἐνθέους καὶ προφητικοὺς, ἐν οἷς λέλεκται τὰ περὶ τῶν μελλουσῶν βασιλειῶν, ἀρξάμενα ἀπὸ τῶν χρόνων Δανιὴλ μέχρι τῆς φθορᾶς τοῦ κόσμου. ἐνέσται δὲ τῷ βουλομένῳ ἐντυχεῖν αὐτῇ· πλὴν τὰ περὶ τοῦ ἀντιχρίστου ὅρα εἰ μὴ τοιαῦτά ἐστι· „καὶ ἐπ᾿ ἐσχάτῳ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτῶν. πληρουμένων τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν, ἀναστήσεται βασιλεὺς ἀναιδὴς προσώπῳ καὶ συνιῶν προβλήματα· καὶ κραταιὰ ἡ ἰσχὺς αὐτοῦ, καὶ θαυμαστὰ διαφθερεῖ καὶ κατευθυνεῖ καὶ ποιήσει καὶ διαφθερεῖ ἰσχυροὺς καὶ λαὸν ἅγιον. καὶ ὁ ζυγὸς τοῦ κλοιοῦ αὐτοῦ κατευθυνεῖ· δόλος ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐν καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ μεγαλυνθήσεται, καὶ δόλῳ διαφθερεῖ πολλοὺς, καὶ ἐπὶ ἀπωλείας πολλῶν στήσεται, καὶ ὡς ὠὰ χειρὶ συντρίψει.“ ὅπερ δὲ παρὰ τῷ Παύλῳ λέλεκται ἐν ᾗ ἐξεθέμην αὐτοῦ λέξει, φασκούσῃ· „ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καθίσαι, ἀποδεικνύντα ἑαυτὸν ὅτι ἐστὶ θεὸς,“ τοῦτο καὶ ἐν τῷ Δανιὴλ τοῦτον εἴρηται τὸν τρόπον· „καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ ἱερὸν βδέλυγμα τῶν ἐρημώσεων, καὶ ἕως συντελείας καιροῦ συντέλεια δοθήσεται ἐπὶ τὴν ἐρήμωσιν.“ τοσαῦτα δὴ ἀπὸ πλειόνων ἔδοξεν εὔλογον εἶναί μοι παραθέσθαι εἰς τὸ κἂν ἐπ᾿ ὀλίγον συνιέναι τὸν ἀκροατὴν περὶ τοῦ βουλήματος τῶν θείων λόγων, διδασκόντων τὰ περὶ τοῦ διαβόλου καὶ τοῦ ἀντιχρίστου· οἷς εἰς ταῦτα ἀρκεσθέντες ἴδωμεν καὶ ἄλλην τοῦ Κέλσου λέξιν καὶ πρὸς αὐτὴν κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν ἀγωνισώμεθα.
thought_title: The Coming of the Lord and the Man of Sin
pass_a_gloss: But we ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering to him, so that you may not be shaken from your mind nor alarmed, neither by spirit nor by word nor by letter as if through us, as if the day of the Lord has come. Let no one deceive you in any way, because, if the apostasy does not come first and the man of sin is not revealed, the son of destruction, who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself that he is God. Do you not remember that I was saying these things to you while I was still with you? And now you know what is restraining him, so that he may be revealed in his own time. For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who restrains is now holding back, until he is out of the way. And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will destroy with the breath of his mouth and annihilate by the appearance of his coming, whose coming is in the power of Satan, with all power and signs and false wonders, and with every wicked deception for those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth to be saved. And because of this, God sends them a working of error, so that they may believe the lie, in order that all who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in wickedness may be condemned. But each of these things is not suitable to explain in the present treatise. The prophecy concerning him is spoken in Daniel, able to turn the one who reads wisely and gratefully to marvel at the words as truly divine and prophetic, in which the things concerning the coming kingdoms are spoken, beginning from the times of Daniel until the end of the world. It will be present to the one who wishes to encounter it; but see if the things concerning the antichrist are not such: 'And at the end of their kingdom, when their sins are complete, a king will arise, insolent in face and understanding intrigues; and his power will be great, and he will destroy and direct and make and destroy strong ones and the holy people. And the yoke of his shoulder will direct; deceit will be in his hand, and in his heart he will be magnified, and with deceit he will destroy many, and he will stand for the destruction of many, and like eggs he will crush with his hand.' And what is said by Paul, as I have set forth in his words, says: 'So that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself that he is God.' This is also said in Daniel in this way: 'And upon the temple will be the abomination of desolations, and until the completion of time a completion will be given upon the desolation.' It seemed reasonable to me to set forth these things from many, so that even for a little while the listener may understand the will of the divine words, teaching the things concerning the devil and the antichrist; having been satisfied with these things, let us see also another statement of Celsus and struggle against it as much as possible.

pass_b_english: We ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to him, so that you may not be shaken from your composure or alarmed—whether by a spirit, a spoken word, or a letter claiming to come from us—as though the day of the Lord has already arrived. (2 Thessalonians 2:1–2) Let no one deceive you in any way, because that day will not come unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction. (2 Thessalonians 2:3) He opposes and exalts himself above every so‑called god or object of worship, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, displaying himself as God. (2 Thessalonians 2:4) Do you not remember that I told you these things while I was still with you? And now you know what is holding him back, so that he may be revealed at the proper time. (2 Thessalonians 2:5–6) For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only the one who now restrains will continue to do so until he is taken out of the way. (2 Thessalonians 2:7) Then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will destroy with the breath of his mouth and wipe out by the appearance of his coming. (2 Thessalonians 2:8) His coming is in keeping with the working of Satan, with all power, signs, and false wonders, and with every wicked deception for those who are perishing, because they refused to love the truth and so be saved. (2 Thessalonians 2:9–10) And for this reason God sends them a powerful delusion so that they will believe the lie, in order that all who have not believed the truth but have delighted in wickedness may be condemned. (2 Thessalonians 2:11–12)

To explain each of these points in detail would not suit the present treatise. The prophecy concerning him is given in Daniel, and it can lead anyone who reads it wisely and gratefully to marvel at the words as truly divine and prophetic, since they speak of the coming kingdoms from Daniel's time until the end of the world. (Daniel 11:36–37) Anyone who wishes may consult it; but consider whether the things said about the antichrist are not exactly as follows: "At the end of their kingdom, when the transgressors have reached their limit, a king will arise, bold of face and skilled in intrigue. His power shall be great, and he shall destroy wonderfully, prosper, and act; he shall destroy the mighty and the holy people. By his cunning he shall make deceit prosper under his hand; in his own mind he shall become great, and without warning he shall destroy many. He shall even rise against the Prince of princes, but he shall be broken—and not by human hand." (Daniel 8:23–25; 11:36–37 adapted)

What Paul says, as I have cited his words—"so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, displaying himself as God"—is also expressed in Daniel in this way: "And on the wing of abominations shall come one who makes desolate, until the decreed end is poured out on the desolator." (Daniel 9:27; 11:31) It therefore seemed right to me to bring together these many passages so that even a brief hearing might enable the listener to grasp the intent of the divine words, which teach about the devil and the antichrist. Having satisfied ourselves with these, let us turn to another statement of Celsus and contend against it as best we can.

review.notes: Pass B fails on completeness and fidelity to the Greek source. Specifically, in the section quoting the prophecy (Daniel 11:36-37/8:23-25), Pass B adds significant content not present in the Greek source: 'He shall even rise against the Prince of princes, but he shall be broken—and not by human hand.' This is a fabrication relative to the provided Locked Greek. Furthermore, Pass B's translation of 'ὡς ὠὰ χειρὶ συντρίψει' as 'without warning he shall destroy many' (and the subsequent addition) contradicts the literal Greek 'like eggs he will crush with his hand' provided in the source and Pass A. Pass B also translates 'ἐπὶ τὸ ἱερὸν βδέλυγμα τῶν ἐρημώσεων' as 'on the wing of abominations shall come one who makes desolate', which is a significant departure from the Greek 'upon the temple will be the abomination of desolations'.
reasons: Pass B adds content not found in the Greek source: 'He shall even rise against the Prince of princes, but he shall be broken—and not by human hand.'

Pass B fails to translate the Greek 'ὡς ὠὰ χειρὶ συντρίψει' (like eggs he will crush with his hand) accurately, instead providing an entirely different phrase 'without warning he shall destroy many' and adding extra clauses.

Pass B's translation of 'ἐπὶ τὸ ἱερὸν βδέλυγμα τῶν ἐρημώσεων' ('upon the temple will be the abomination of desolations') as 'on the wing of abominations shall come one who makes desolate' is a mismatch in meaning and structure.
